scope: Finish development tuning, held-out product comparison, randomized-start sensitivity, and small PG comparison before any Stage D decision.
replication: Full prescribed problem-seed by stochastic-seed product for stochastic methods. Deterministic product-start methods run once per dataset. Randomized panel uses five distinct matched initialization/stochastic-seed pairs per dataset, including deterministic methods because their initial states differ.
tuning_budget_rationale: Section 12 permits a prospectively fixed development budget. All candidates receive 10 solver seconds on every required development cell; selected primary trajectories provide both 30- and 300-second opportunities without duplicate 30-second reruns.
oracle_selection_scope: Fixed initial candidate from prior development diagnostics, not a claim of stochastic speed benefit.
inner_setting_note: Applies to custom KL and Dykstra. Native POT inner settings remain unchanged; its Sinkhorn default is not overridden or inferred from warnings.

pg.tolerance_metric: projection primal-dual gap, not marginal residual

candidate_ids: c00 through c11 in JSON grid-axis order; exact numeric score ties use lexicographic candidate ID.

selection.score: flat median over all prescribed run cells of final_float64_rounded_loss / canonical_product_plan_loss_float64
selection.normalization: Each run is normalized by its own frozen instance's product-plan loss; equal repetition counts per instance prevent scale or replication weighting differences.
selection.run_failure: missing run, status failed, mismatched inputs, nonfinite final score, invalid rounded output, or missing required final float64 evidence
selection.candidate_failure: Any required run failure makes the candidate ineligible and its score positive infinity; failures cannot be hidden by the median.
selection.inner_failure_policy: Completed runs with inner iteration caps or native warnings remain eligible if their actual rounded outputs validate. Retain and report all failures, residuals, warnings and unknown native inner counts.
selection.native_early_stop: A valid native final output before the nominal budget remains eligible; report actual solver time and missing later checkpoint windows.
selection.tie_break: exact numeric equality, then lexicographic candidate ID; no arbitrary tolerance
selection.all_ineligible: Emit no_valid_setting, stop final-manifest generation for review, and never select a fallback.
selection.heldout_access: Finalize and archive selection before generating or running held-out final manifests; no parameter changes based on held-out values.

small_pg_context: Held-out n=128, both noise levels, selected PG and previously selected full-KL plus parameter-free FW, 30-second matched panel. No 300-second small-PG claim.
exact_smoothing_ablation: Inherit the selected stochastic smoothing constants and replace only the oracle by the exact gradient. Do not retune, duplicate deterministic product starts, or invoke Proposition 2.12.
dedicated_theory_configuration: The existing gamma0=rho0=1, mu_scale=1 theorem track remains separate from the selected practical configurations.
randomized_initialization: 0.9*a*b^T+0.1*R/n; private default_rng(init_seed); same permutation across methods. Native Sampled GW excluded because its initialization remains fixed.
device_policy: one A100 per independent run; float32; AMP off; highest matmul precision; TF32 off; deterministic CUBLAS; one CPU thread per runner
budget_caveat: These are nominal solver budgets, not elapsed runtime predictions. Diagnostics, initialization/iteration overshoot, serialization, scheduler queue time and failures add overhead; native early stops may reduce solver time.
stage_d: Not part of this campaign. Lack of pilot advantage does not excuse unfinished Stage C tuning or replication; decide scaling only from completed evidence.
